clue.text: Number in favour of surrounding university

indicators.note: surrounding tells us one piece is placed around another, enclosing it

parts.note: being for something means being in favour of it

explanation.surface: A figure supporting a campus cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Four is an example of a number, the integer after three.

clue.text: Delivered popular short film on time to cutter

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular, as in the in crowd

indicators.note: short means the word is cut back by its final letter

parts.note: a flick is an informal word for a film
a film editor cuts footage, so a cutter is an editor, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: A trendy short movie was handed to the editor in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' looks like a tool or boat but is a film editor, ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver a blow is to inflict it, so delivered and inflicted are synonyms in that sense.

indicators.note: reserves here means keeps or holds back, so one piece holds another within it

parts.note: else means other or different, as in someone else
AP is an abbreviation of apparently

explanation.surface: Seemingly distinct reserve forces pass through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserves' looks like a noun for back-up troops but is a verb meaning holds: ELSE holds AP.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that goes by is said to pass or slip away; the two phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: Near a swimmer, keeping very quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a roach is a freshwater fish, a swimmer
PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: Someone close to a person swimming, staying hushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' is a fish, the roach, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to near something is to come closer to it; the two verbs are synonyms.

parts.note: 18 and 26 give POEM and EASTER, so the clue points to Yeats's poem Easter, 1916, whose refrain says something self-contradictory is born

explanation.surface: A contradiction in terms that came to life in a 1916 poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Yeats's poem Easter, 1916 has the refrain that a contradictory phrase 'is born'; the phrase pairs dreadful with lovely, hence an oxymoron.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted phrase joins opposites, dreadful and lovely, which is exactly what an oxymoron does.

clue.text: Powerful society passes round Republican signs

indicators.note: to pass round something is to encircle it, so these letters go around another

parts.note: potent means powerful

explanation.surface: A strong society hands out republican symbols.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passes round' suggests distributing, but here POTENT plus S goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Portents are omens, signs warning of what is to come.

indicators.note: 10-across gives RISING, and in a down clue rising means reading upwards, backwards
limited by means confined within, so the letters lie hidden inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A beginning hemmed in by ten pet hates.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a number but stands for its solution, RISING; in a down clue that reverses TESNO, hidden in 'bêtes noires'.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the beginning of something, as in the onset of winter.

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or said, so the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: a canon is a churchman, and aids means assists; together they are said aloud

explanation.surface: Word has it a clergyman helps out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannonade is a sustained barrage of artillery fire, a bout of shelling.

indicators.note: over here means covering, so one piece sits over and around the other
mostly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: to stand something is to bear or suffer it
a rag is a disparaging term for a tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: Barely tolerating a gutter paper's franchise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'franchise' is not a business licence here but the right to vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Franchise in its political sense is the right to vote, the same meaning as suffrage.

definitions.note: 10 is the solution of 10-across, RISING, used as a noun here

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: fills means goes inside, so these letters are placed within others

parts.note: a section is a part of something
U stands for upper class, socially superior
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A senior bishop takes a role in the Rising.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' means the solution of 10-across, RISING.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising in the sense of a revolt is an uprising, a synonym for an armed rebellion.

clue.text: Offers made by very resolute rebels about noon

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round another
rebels suggests the letters rise up and break order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Very determined insurgents make proposals around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebels' looks like a noun but signals an anagram of RESOLUTE, which goes 'about' N. The Irish Volunteers were rebels of 1916.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer is to offer oneself or something freely, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Small aristo dislodges line of police in 10's General HQ

indicators.note: to dislodge is to push something out of its place, so one letter of the police word is ousted and replaced

parts.note: taken as written
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a toff is a slang word for an upper-class person, an aristocrat

explanation.surface: A minor nobleman displaces a cordon of officers at the Rising's headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' refers to the RISING of 10-across. 'dislodges' means S and TOFF push out the L of POLICE and take its place.
explanation.definitionFit: During the Easter Rising of 1916, the rebels made the General Post Office in Dublin's Sackville Street their headquarters.

clue.text: Old carrier left to absorb another one in bad faith

indicators.note: to absorb is to take inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: BEA, British European Airways, was a former British airline, an old carrier
a tray is another kind of carrier, for food or drinks

explanation.surface: A defunct airline took over a rival in a double-cross.
explanation.walkthrough: BEA was a British airline merged into British Airways in 1974. 'carrier' shifts from airline to tray.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal is treachery, the breaking of trust, which is acting in bad faith.

clue.text: Colonists jail special "heirs of 1916", ambitious types

indicators.note: to jail is to lock up inside, so these letters enclose others

parts.note: ants live in colonies, so they are colonists
the IRA, Irish Republican Army, claims descent from the rebels of 1916

explanation.surface: Settlers imprison the political heirs of the Easter rebels, who are pushy people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colonists' are not settlers but ants, which live in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirants are people who aspire to something, ambitious hopefuls.

clue.text: Curse a rioting man stealing articles

indicators.note: stealing means taking something in, so these letters hold others
rioting means running wild and disorderly, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: a and the are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: Damn a rampaging man who is pilfering goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' looks like goods but means the grammatical articles A and THE, taken inside NMA, the anagram of MAN from 'rioting'.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal ecclesiastical curse, or more loosely a thing detested.

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: a guy is a chap, a man
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A man collected a ball, showing good control, as in football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' is a formal dance, not a football.
explanation.definitionFit: Guidance is direction or steering, a sense of control as in a missile's guidance system.

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American author
M stands for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A writer annotates Yeats's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marks' looks like annotations but is the currency abbreviation M.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeats wrote verse; Easter, 1916 is one example of his writing in verse.

indicators.note: abandoned by means left by, so one letter departs from the word

parts.note: a device is a plan or scheme

explanation.surface: A plan dropped by the English.
explanation.walkthrough: '17' points to the solution of 17-across, GUIDANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is counsel offered to help someone decide, which is a form of guidance.

indicators.note: flounders means struggles clumsily, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A market trader sold bad flatfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flounders' reads as fish but is a verb signalling the anagram. A barrow boy is a British market seller who trades from a wheeled cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrow boy is a man who sells goods from a cart in the street, a hawker.

clue.text: In 1607 they fled opposing sides in stormy sea

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other letters
stormy means turbulent, so the letters are churned up

parts.note: right and left are opposite sides, R and L

explanation.surface: Fleeing across a rough sea in 1607.
explanation.walkthrough: The Flight of the Earls in 1607 saw the Gaelic lords of Ulster flee Ireland by sea. 'stormy' makes EAS of SEA, with RL put 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flight of the Earls was the departure of Ulster's Gaelic nobility to continental Europe in 1607.

indicators.note: a helping is a portion, so a portion of the word Paisley gives the letters

explanation.surface: The Northern Irish politician Ian Paisley is lending Ireland a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Paisley was a fiercely unionist Northern Irish leader, which makes him 'helping Ireland' a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is an island, an example of an isle, hence the 'perhaps'.

indicators.note: guarding means keeping inside protectively, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: per se means essentially, in itself

explanation.surface: The head of the Rising is fundamentally defending territory.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' points to the solution of 10-across, RISING.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrick Pearse read the Proclamation of the Irish Republic and commanded the rebels of 1916.

clue.text: Loyal politician, one controlling working lives

indicators.note: controlling suggests holding or containing, so one piece goes round the others

parts.note: a unit is one, a single thing
on means working or operating, as a machine is on
is means exists or lives

explanation.surface: A faithful MP is one who governs working lives.
explanation.walkthrough: In Northern Ireland a loyalist politician wants to keep the union with Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A unionist in Northern Ireland supports staying in the United Kingdom, loyal to the British Crown.

clue.text: I call for help and stay working for balanced state

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal, a call for help

indicators.note: working means being worked on and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sends a distress call and keeps going to stay level.
explanation.walkthrough: Isostasy is a geology term: the earth's crust floats in equilibrium on the denser mantle beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology, isostasy is the equilibrium of the crust floating on the mantle, an equilibrium of masses.

clue.text: "Erin is great!" — slogan originally spread by its leaders?

definitions.text: "Erin is great!" — slogan originally spread by its leaders?

indicators.note: spread here means scattered about, so the letters of the quoted cry are dispersed and rearranged
originally points to the opening letter of the word slogan

explanation.surface: A patriotic cry for Ireland is spread abroad by the leaders of a movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the rebel leaders of 1916 spread a cry for Ireland's greatness. Erin is a poetic name for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1916 rebellion in Dublin against British rule, led by Pearse and others, whose leaders proclaimed Irish independence.
